notes.content: You know that feeling — you can see exactly what's wrong, but you still can't make it right. That's a specific kind of stuck, isn't it? Jehovah actually names it right here in Jeremiah 4:22. He says his people are 'clever enough when it comes to doing bad, but they do not know how to do good.' Not that they couldn't identify good — they'd been hearing from prophets for years. The problem was skill without surrender. You know how a mechanic can diagnose every fault code on your dad's transmission but still hand it back broken? That's not an ignorance problem — that's a will problem. Now look at Proverbs 1:7 — 'the fear of Jehovah is the beginning of wisdom.' Not the knowledge of Jehovah. The fear. That's the part that converts clever into capable. So if you walked in here today feeling like you already know the material — that's not enough, and you already know that. What you walk out with is permission: the distance between knowing and doing closes the moment reverence takes the wheel.
